title: In-vehicle Register for Heavy Vehicles to Record Exceeding of Speed Limit
what_it_is: In-vehicle Register for Heavy Vehicles to Record Exceeding of Speed Limit

sections.label: Heavy vehicle speeding penalties
sections.summary: Passage states penalties for heavy vehicle speeding, speed limiter tampering, and that TP and LTA are reviewing measures.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: Heavy vehicles with speed limiters are also required to undergo additional speed limiter inspections, if these vehicles were caught speeding.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: Those caught tampering with their speed limiters can be fined up to $1,000 or imprisoned up to three months, while repeat offenders can be fined up to $2,000 or imprisoned up to six months.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: Heavy vehicle drivers caught exceeding the speed limit by up to 40 kilometres per hour will be given composition fines ranging from $160 to $200 and four to eight demerit points.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: Heavy vehicle drivers caught exceeding the speed limit by more than 40 kilometres per hour will be charged in court and given 12 to 24 demerit points.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: The Traffic Police (TP) and the Land and Transport Authority (LTA) are reviewing measures to curb heavy vehicle speeding and will announce the changes later this year.

sections.label: Review of curbing problem
sections.summary: Passage states hope that implementation or a review will take place to curb the problem, and that it will be taken onboard.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I am hopeful that this can be implemented or at least, a review will take place to make sure that we can curb this problem.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: We will take that onboard when we review.
